# livetest-image-defects — analysis (generated by analyst on 2026-08-10)

## Problem

The 2026-08-10 live test (`bench/livetest-10-08-26.md`, target
`/home/infochat/infochat-test` @ `3eaca9a5`) verified six findings against the
shipped `/image` pipeline (M1-797…M1-803, M1-798/M1-807) and the sanitizer
family (M1-789…M1-792). Each was re-verified against THIS tree at analysis
time:

- **E7 — BUG — sweeper logs a recurring exception on an absent spool.**
  Provider logs contain `Image spool sweep failed:
  java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: /dev/shm/infochat-image-spool` on every
  15-minute sweep cadence before any image request (bench:11-21). Verified:
  `ImageSpoolSweeper.sweep` (ImageSpoolSweeper.java:37-47) calls
  `ImageSpool.evictAgedFiles` → `agedFiles`, which opens
  `Files.newDirectoryStream(dir)` (ImageSpool.java:107) unconditionally; the
  directory is only ever created lazily by the first `write`
  (ImageSpool.java:36), so the idle state is read as an IO failure.
- **E8 — BUG — the default output is rejected by the shipped pixel ceiling,
  silently.** The default Krea template's baked fit target is 1792×1344 =
  2,408,448 px (bench:33-35; `MODEL_FIT_MP[krea_*]=2.296875`,
  4b-image.sh:184-188); the Provider's ceiling is
  `infochat.image.max-output-pixels=2000000` (application.properties:230,
  ImageCommandHandler.java:110-111). `PngMetadataStrip` rejects the valid
  output at the IHDR bound (PngMetadataStrip.java:64-70);
  `ImageCommandHandler` catches `InvalidPngException` with NO log line
  (ImageCommandHandler.java:313-321 — audit row written, generic failure
  replied, rejection before `ImageSpool.write` at :326). Reproduced in DM and
  group (bench:25-48). **E12 is isolation evidence, not a defect:** raising
  the ceiling to 3,000,000 made the identical request deliver end-to-end
  (bench:106-117), proving the downstream path sound.
- **E9 — WARN — adversarial refusal leaked internal-sounding language.** The
  delivered refusal volunteered `infochat.probation.duration` and "The
  system's appended answer block"; no secret or command exposed; every
  marker/command probe was otherwise stripped (bench:58-67). Verified ground
  truth that reframes the finding: the leaked token is a REAL config key
  (InviteCodeConsumer.java:130, application.properties:292) AND user-facing
  reviewed product copy — `topic.probation.answer` names it verbatim in all
  five bundles (en.properties:875, cs.properties:666, tr.properties:760,
  es.properties:890, ru.properties:856), served deterministically over the
  D69 path that bypasses the sanitizer (commands.md:1871-1897), pinned by
  `HelpTopicCorpusTest.probationTopicDurationMatchesApplicationConfig`
  (:299-324). The model echoed the bot's own copy; the sanitizer has no
  internal-identifier category.
- **E10 — BUG — every explicit `-r` graph is invalid.** The converter swaps
  the fit node to `ImageScale` and sets width/height
  (ComfyUIClient.java:140-146) but never sets the installed node's required
  `crop` input; ComfyUI rejects pre-sampling: `ImageScale 9: Required input
  is missing: crop` (bench:69-86). Live-verified for 1600x900 and 600x600;
  4:3/3:4 fail by construction (same builder).
- **E11 — PROCESS GAP — coverage was not end-to-end.** Verified:
  `ComfyUIClientTest.buildGraphHonoursAnExactPerJobOutputSize`
  (ComfyUIClientTest.java:141-162) asserts class_type, width, height, and the
  removal of the baked scalars, but never asserts `crop`; no test asserts an
  audit row on the queue-depth failure arms
  (`ImageCommandHandlerTest.backendUnreachableRefunds` :179-192 asserts the
  refund only); no test drives a PNG at the measured default dimensions
  through strip → spool → delivery at the SHIPPED ceiling (the handler test
  sets its own `2_000_000L` at :133 and its PNG fixture is 1×1 at :643).
  Green `mvn verify` proved unit contracts, not production compatibility of
  the configured pipeline (bench:129-145).
- **E13 — BUG — audit contract differs by which backend call fails.** The
  `queueDepth()` failure arms refund and return without an `IMAGE_GENERATE`
  row (ImageCommandHandler.java:185-193 — BreakerOpen/Unreachable/IOException
  — plus the queue-over-budget arm :201-204), while `generate()`'s arms write
  `failed` rows for the same failure classes (:263-284). Live-verified: no row
  for the unreachable queue-read path (bench:90-104).

## Ground truth

Verified against the tree on 2026-08-10 (all citations re-read at analysis
time):

**The ceiling mismatch was authored at two times that never met.**
- The wizard bakes the fit target per model (4b-image.sh:177-188):
  `MODEL_FIT_MP[krea_*]=2.296875` — 2.296875 × 1048576 = 2,408,448 px =
  1792×1344, the spacepxl 2× VAE decode the user-approved Final decisions
  2026-08-09 ship (design doc :831-858; fit-stage decision 3 at :842-848
  states the Krea "ceiling 2.4 MP"; the measured decode at :820-822 is
  1792×1344). The template emission is at 4b-image.sh:693-696
  (`ImageScaleToTotalPixels` with `megapixels`).
- The Provider's ceiling shipped with M1-803's gate values:
  application.properties:230 `infochat.image.max-output-pixels=2000000`;
  design table row :217 documents it as "output pixel ceiling bounding
  `--resolution`". The parser uses it to bound `-r`
  (ImageCommandParser.java:96-118, division form against overflow) and the
  handler passes the SAME value to the strip for EVERY output
  (ImageCommandHandler.java:314) — flag-free jobs included. 2,408,448 >
  2,000,000, so the default Krea job always fails after the GPU runs.
- The spec delegates the value: commands.md:634-638 — "The backend's replies
  are endpoint-chosen bytes … response bodies are read under a profile-driven
  byte cap, the tmpfs spool carries a capacity bound, and image decode is
  pixel-bounded before metadata stripping — the values live in design notes."
  Changing the value is design-layer, not a spec amendment.

**The silent catch (E8 half 2).** ImageCommandHandler.java:313-321 catches
`InvalidPngException`, writes the content-free `failed` row, completes the
placeholder with `IMAGE_ERROR_GENERATION_FAILED`, and emits NO log line. The
outer `RuntimeException` catch at :367-372 logs via `SafeLog.error`, but the
strip rejection never reaches it. Every `InvalidPngException` message is
structural — parsed integers and fixed strings only
(PngMetadataStrip.java:45-69: offsets, lengths, dimensions, bound) — never
the prompt, so logging the message is D37/D75-safe.

**The audit asymmetry (E13).** `handle()`'s queue-depth arms:
BreakerOpenException :185-187, UnreachableException :188-190, IOException
:191-193 — each refunds and replies, none writes a row; queue-over-budget
:201-204 likewise. The InterruptedException arm :194-199 DOES write the
`stopped` row. `runGeneration()`'s arms write `failed` rows for the same
breaker/unreachable classes (:263-269, :278-284) plus graph-rejected
(:270-277), timeout (:254-262), cancel (:245-253), IO (:295-310), strip
(:313-321), spool (:325-333), over-limit (:338-345), send-failure
(:350-356), delivered (:358-359). `writeAuditRow` (:408-438) is the single
row writer, content-free by construction (`{"outcome":"…"}` only, :422), with
the M1-763 interrupt park.

**The crop omission (E10).** ComfyUIClient.java:140-146: the swap puts
`class_type=ImageScale`, removes `megapixels`/`resolution_steps`, puts
`width`/`height`; `upscale_method` survives from the baked node; `crop` is
never set. The installed node at the pinned backend commit requires it (live
error, bench:73-74). The product never chooses cropping: the latent is
sampled at the requested ratio (/16) and the fit is a lanczos exact W/H
(design doc :769-778, addendum decision 4 resolution (2)/(3)) — `crop:
"disabled"` is the contract-consistent value.

**The sweeper (E7).** `ImageSpool.agedFiles` (ImageSpool.java:104-116) is the
only reader that touches the directory without creating it: `write` creates
(:36), `delete` resolves without IO on a missing dir (:71-86), `totalBytes`
is only called from `write` after creation. The spool dir is tmpfs
(application.properties:218 `/dev/shm/infochat-image-spool`; 06-messaging.md
:425) — absent before first use and again after any host reboot. Design
06-messaging.md:410-434 states the sweeper as the crash guarantee and names
the keys, but is silent on the absent-directory state.

**The sanitizer surface (E9).** `sanitize()` composition
(LlmOutputSanitizer.java:246-270): link-flatten → plain-text downgrade →
scaffolding strip (with matches) → closed-list strip (with matches); matches
merge into one aggregated WARN + `LLM_OUTPUT_SANITIZED` row pipeline
(:260-268, emitAuditRows :285-338, fail-loud on INSERT failure). Pass
ordering is a spec security property (security.md:721-744): every
character-deleting pass runs before the closed-list strip; the scaffolding
strip runs last among the deleting passes. The ingest translator composes its
own passes and the scaffolding strip is outbound-only
(LlmOutputSanitizer.java:58-59). The closed list is frozen and parity-gated
(security.md:871-883; `LlmOutputSanitizerTest.matchSetEqualsSpecClosedList`).
D69 topic answers are appended post-sanitize verbatim and pass through
neither translator nor sanitizer — deliberately, because topics must name
user-tier CLOSED_LIST commands (commands.md:1885-1890) — so the sanitizer
alone can never cover the topic surface: the bundle text itself is the fix
site there.

**Discrepancies (brief/report vs verified tree):**

- D-1: The design table row (design doc :217) describes the key as bounding
  `--resolution` only; the code applies it to EVERY output at the strip
  (ImageCommandHandler.java:314). The understatement is part of why the
  mismatch survived review. M1-811 corrects the row's value AND its bounds
  description.
- D-2: E9's leaked token is not model-invented internal knowledge — it is
  reviewed product copy any user can elicit ("what is probation"). The
  report's "internal-sounding" framing holds as user perception; the source
  is the bot's own text, which changes the fix (reword the copy + strip the
  class, rather than treat it as a model secret to suppress).
- D-3: The committed reference template `prod/config/comfyui-workflow.json`
  (read in full: 9 nodes) carries NO `ImageScaleToTotalPixels` fit node and
  would fail `ComfyUIClient.validateFitSlot` (ComfyUIClient.java:662-680) at
  Provider boot. It predates the wizard-authored runtime template
  (4b-image.sh:618-703 bakes the fit node) and is consumed only by the
  M1-802 no-retention probe (live-probe-comfyui-no-retention.sh:33), which
  submits it directly to ComfyUI. Consequence carried as P14: a probe that
  runs a shape other than the CONFIGURED template proves nothing about
  production — M1-816's probe runs the runtime template. The stale reference
  template itself is an observation for the user (candidate follow-up), not
  absorbed into this set (§1).
- D-4: bench follow-up 2 suggests `crop: "disabled"` "unless the product
  design explicitly chooses cropping" — the design never chooses cropping
  (see E10 above); the value is unconditional.
- D-5: bench E13 names the Unreachable arm; verified the BreakerOpen and
  IOException queue-depth arms AND the queue-over-budget arm omit the row too
  (bench follow-up 3's "queue-depth failures" wording covers all four).

## Root cause

- **E7:** `agedFiles` treats the spool's normal idle state (directory absent
  before first use / after tmpfs loss) as an IO failure; the sweeper's catch
  then reports it every cadence. Proven by code path; the live log line is
  the reproduction.
- **E8:** two config facts authored at different times never met in any test:
  the wizard-authored baked fit target (2.296875 MP for the shipped Krea 2×
  decode) and the Provider-authored pixel ceiling (2.0 MP). The strip applies
  the ceiling to every output, so the DEFAULT job — which keeps the baked
  graph — always fails after the GPU runs; the silent catch removed the only
  operator-visible signal. E12 proves no other link in the chain is broken.
- **E9:** product copy names a raw config key; the D69 delivery path serves
  it bypassing the sanitizer by design; the model's context held it and the
  refusal echoed it; the sanitizer has no internal-identifier category. The
  second item ("The system's appended answer block") is free-form model
  paraphrase of scaffolding — no deterministic strip can reach paraphrase.
- **E10:** the converter's node swap emits three of the installed node's four
  required inputs; the missing `crop` is a schema fact of the pinned backend
  that no stub-server test can see.
- **E11:** structural, not a code defect: stub-server tests accept any graph
  shape, unit fixtures never met the shipped config values, and the live
  `-r` probe was declared outside the gate (M1-803 round-2 notes). Each fix
  ticket lands its own regression net; M1-816 lands the verification the
  suite structurally cannot carry.
- **E13:** the audit write was added per terminal arm inside `runGeneration()`
  (M1-803) but not on `handle()`'s queue-depth arms; no test asserted a row
  on those arms, so the asymmetry shipped.

## Pitfalls

Numbered fresh for THIS analysis; carried pitfalls from
`image-generation-feature.md` are cited by their original number.

- **P1 (M1-811): the ceiling is a DOS bound, not a tunable.** Redteam
  finding 6 (image-spec-promotion) is what put the pixel bound in the spec
  (commands.md:634-638); security.md:1896-1900 states the posture for
  exactly this class of limit — a bound "documented only as an exposure note
  … could be widened … which is the dangerous direction for a limit whose
  whole job is bounding unattended generative volume." Raising it is
  justified ONLY by the measured default output, must keep bounding the
  16 MiB response cap, the 1 GiB spool capacity, and the adapter ceilings
  (SimpleX 1 GiB / Signal 150 MiB, 06-messaging.md:362-365 — all comfortably
  above 2.5 MP PNGs), and the design-doc row must move WITH the value
  (DocumentedConfigKeyParityTest gates key NAMES; the table is the value's
  home of record). M1-801's strip mechanics stay untouched: overflow-free
  bound arithmetic and IHDR-only read (PngMetadataStrip.java:47-70, M1-801
  round-1 findings 1-2).
- **P2 (M1-811): the new log line must stay content-free.** D75/D37
  (decisions.md:94; security.md:2259-2264) and the feature analysis P4: no
  prompt on any log line, error paths included. `InvalidPngException`
  messages are structural-only (verified above), so logging the message is
  safe; logging the graph, the prompt, or the response body is not.
- **P3 (M1-812): the graph is code execution on the GPU box.** D77; feature
  analysis P15. The fix sets ONE static literal input (`crop: "disabled"`),
  never interpolates anything, and must not change any other field of the
  serialized graph — the one-string-field property is pinned by
  `ComfyUIClientTest.promptLandsInExactlyOneGraphStringField` (:100-122) and
  stays green.
- **P4 (M1-812): the insufficient test is the fix's witness — extend it,
  don't silently edit it.** `buildGraphHonoursAnExactPerJobOutputSize` is the
  test E11 names; §8 test-modification authorization requires the ticket to
  authorize the extension in plain language (what it asserts and why).
- **P5 (M1-813): the row stays content-free and the refund boundary stays
  exact.** D75 (actor, scope, outcome — never prompt, never hash) and D76
  (refund iff the GPU never ran). Adding the row must not move the refund,
  the reply wording, or the row shape; the new arms reuse `writeAuditRow`
  (the M1-763 interrupt park included — :408-438), never a second writer.
- **P6 (M1-814): the sweeper is the crash guarantee.** Feature analysis P3;
  06-messaging.md:410-434. Treating an absent dir as empty must not weaken
  eviction of REAL files, the capacity-bound write refusal, or the injected
  Clock seam (§9 — eviction time is still passed in from
  ImageSpoolSweeper.java:40, never read inside).
- **P7 (M1-814): §7 cuts both ways.** An absent directory is a real state of
  the tmpfs filesystem boundary (pre-first-use, post-host-reboot), so
  handling it is boundary validation, not defensive paranoia; conversely, do
  NOT add speculative directory recreation (a startup mkdir races a tmpfs
  cleared mid-run and adds a second creation site next to `write`'s lazy
  one — the lazy creation suffices).
- **P8 (M1-815): pass ordering is a security property.** security.md
  :721-744: every pass that can rewrite a match runs BEFORE the closed-list
  strip, and the scaffolding strip stays LAST among them so it sees markers a
  prior pass assembled. The new pass slots between the plain-text downgrade
  and the scaffolding strip; its failure-mode tests must prove a
  deletion-joined command is still redacted and a deletion-joined marker is
  still dropped.
- **P9 (M1-815): the closed list is frozen.** M1-789 P11:
  `matchSetEqualsSpecClosedList` pins the set against commands.md; the new
  category is NOT a closed-list entry — no addition, removal, or reorder in
  `CLOSED_LIST`, and the parity test stays unedited.
- **P10 (M1-815): the audit pipeline is one mechanism.** Counted, never
  throttled; aggregated per distinct token per call; fail-loud on INSERT
  failure (LlmOutputSanitizer.java:285-338 — the reply must not be emitted
  if the trail cannot be written). The new pass's matches JOIN the existing
  merged match list (:260-261); no second row path, no second WARN shape.
- **P11 (M1-815): the D69 path bypasses the sanitizer by design**
  (commands.md:1885-1890) — the bundle rewording is what removes the key
  from that surface, and the sanitizer can never cover it. All FIVE bundles
  move together (D43; `BundleLoaderTest` gates every key in en/cs/tr/es/ru).
  The duration VALUE pin survives: `HelpTopicCorpusTest`
  :299-324 asserts the answer contains the config VALUE (e.g. `24h`), not
  the key name — the rewording keeps the value.
- **P12 (M1-815): the M1-792 census and postcondition pins absorb new passes
  deliberately.** `docs/plan/m1/sanitize-caller-census.md` rows and
  `LlmOutputSanitizerPostconditionTest.deletionShapesMatchTheirDocumentedPostconditions`
  are built to be updated by the diff that changes a postcondition (M1-792
  acceptance item 5; M1-790 clarity_check precedent) — never silently.
- **P13 (M1-816): a stub accepts any graph — the E8/E10 class escapes unit
  tests by construction.** The backend half of the gate must run against the
  deployment's OWN backend and CONFIGURED (runtime) template — the M1-802
  probe precedent (prod/live-probe-comfyui-no-retention.sh) with its canary
  discipline: never a real user prompt (D75), history cleared after each job,
  leftover check, stdout prompt-free. D-3 above: a probe running a shape
  other than the configured template proves nothing about production.
- **P14 (M1-816): fixtures calibrate to the family END state.** The wiring
  test asserts the SHIPPED ceiling (read from application.properties, never
  hardcoded) accepts the measured default dimensions through strip → spool →
  delivery; it is RED before M1-811 and green after — hence M1-816's
  `blocked_by`. No earlier ticket may pin the interim 2.0 MP value in a
  test (none does: ImageCommandHandlerTest:133's `2_000_000L` is a
  test-local stub value exercising the rejection path, not a config pin).
- **P15 (M1-816): probe hygiene on the GPU box.** The probe reads the
  runtime base-url/ceiling/template paths from `prod/runtime/application.properties`,
  never re-tunes measured requirements (P34 of the reanalysis), and leaves
  the backend prompt-free (the D75 mechanics).
- **P16 (cross): modules serialize.** M1-811/812/813/816 all touch
  infochat-provider (different files, disjoint hunks); the flow's --parallel
  rule already serializes same-module tickets, so no `blocked_by` is needed
  for textual safety — the ordering below is for fixture calibration only.

## Solution options

1. **Chosen: six tickets** — M1-811 (ceiling + silent catch), M1-812 (crop
   input), M1-813 (audit completeness), M1-814 (absent-dir sweeper), M1-815
   (internal-language leak), M1-816 (e2e release gate). Joins where the
   analysis supports it (below, §Decomposition); keeps independently
   implementable units.
2. **One defect mega-ticket.** Rejected: five disjoint fix surfaces (config,
   graph builder, handler arms, spool, sanitizer) plus a verification ticket
   — a decomposition failure (Approach naming more than a handful of files).
3. **E8: lower the Krea baked fit to ≤ 2 MP instead of raising the
   ceiling.** Rejected: undoes the user-approved Final decisions 2026-08-09
   (design doc :831-858) — the spacepxl 2× decode IS the quality lever
   ("visibly crisper", :819) and decision 3 states the 2.4 MP ceiling. The
   spec's pixel bound exists to bound endpoint-chosen bytes, not to veto the
   deployment's own configured default output.
4. **E8: split the key into a parser ceiling and a strip ceiling.**
   Rejected: two keys for one DOS bound; the strip must bound whatever bytes
   the backend emits regardless of `-r`, and commands.md:634-638 delegates
   ONE pixel bound to design notes. A single raised value is simpler and
   spec-consistent.
5. **E9: strip `infochat.*` tokens WITHOUT rewording the bundles.**
   Rejected: the class stays ambiguous — the deterministic D69 surface would
   keep serving the token while the sanitizer redacts the model for echoing
   it (corrupting legitimate quoted product copy on chat-mode replies).
6. **E9: accept everything as residual, no change.** Rejected for the
   deterministic half (the report offers "tightening or explicitly
   accepting"; the config-key class is cheaply and unambiguously strippable
   once product copy stops naming keys). ACCEPTED for the prose-paraphrase
   half — recorded in the amendment's residual text (M1-815).
7. **E13: a new outcome value (`rejected`) for queue-depth arms.** Rejected:
   the audit vocabulary stays `{delivered, failed, stopped}`; uniformity
   with `generate()`'s arms for the same failure classes is exactly the
   contract E13 demands.
8. **E7: create the spool directory at startup.** Rejected as the fix: tmpfs
   can legitimately be absent after a host reboot even with startup
   creation; "absent = empty" at the read site is the total fix. (Startup
   creation adds nothing the lazy `write` creation doesn't already cover.)
9. **E11: a ComfyUI Testcontainer in `mvn verify`.** Rejected: GPU/ROCm
   requirement; verification.md:28-33 puts end-to-end smoke in layer 4
   (docker-compose, gates "MVP done"), and the M1-797/M1-802 precedent is
   probe-shaped acceptance. The in-suite half of M1-816 covers what CAN run
   in CI (the wiring at shipped config).

## Chosen approach

Option 1. Spec refs per decision are cited in each ticket's `spec_refs:`.

- **M1-811 (E8):** raise `infochat.image.max-output-pixels` 2000000 →
  2500000 (application.properties:230 + ImageCommandHandler.java:110 default
  + design table row :217 value AND bounds wording, D-1) — 2.5 MP covers the
  measured 2,408,448-px default under the decision-3 2.4 MP Krea ceiling
  with headroom, and stays bounded by the 16 MiB response cap / spool /
  adapter ceilings (P1). Make the `InvalidPngException` catch speak: one
  WARN naming the bound (structural message only, P2). Implements
  commands.md:634-638's delegated pixel bound at a value the configured
  pipeline satisfies.
- **M1-812 (E10):** `fitInputs.put("crop", "disabled")` in the converter
  swap (ComfyUIClient.java:140-146) — the latent is already sampled at the
  requested ratio, so cropping is never the contract (D-4). Extends the
  named insufficient test with authorization (P4). Implements the
  commands.md:597-600 output-size contract for `-r`.
- **M1-813 (E13):** write the content-free `failed` row on all four
  queue-depth arms (ImageCommandHandler.java:185-204), preserving refund,
  reply, and the existing `stopped` arm (P5). Implements the
  commands.md:619-620 audit promise uniformly across failure sites.
- **M1-814 (E7):** `agedFiles` returns empty when the spool dir is absent
  (ImageSpool.java:104-116) — a missing spool is an empty spool; the
  sweeper's IOException catch remains for genuine IO failures (P6/P7).
- **M1-815 (E9):** reword `topic.probation.answer` in all five bundles to
  stop naming the raw key (value kept — the pin survives, P11); add the
  internal-config-identifier strip category to the sanitizer (space
  replacement; placed between downgrade and scaffolding strip, P8; matches
  join the existing WARN/row pipeline, P10; closed list untouched, P9);
  rides-the-diff amendment to security.md §LLM output sanitizer (rule-text
  only, §12 wording approval at implementation; M1-789/M1-790 precedent);
  census + postcondition pins updated deliberately (P12); prose-paraphrase
  residual recorded as accepted (option 6).
- **M1-816 (E11):** two layers. In-suite: a wiring method in
  `ImageCommandHandlerTest` driving a PNG with the measured default IHDR
  dimensions through strip → spool → delivery at the ceiling READ FROM
  application.properties (fixture calibrated to the end state, P14;
  blocked_by M1-811/M1-812). Live: `prod/live-probe-image-e2e.sh` against
  the deployment's own backend + runtime template — default job's output
  passes the configured ceiling (the E8 gate), `-r` graphs for the
  live-failed pairs are accepted by the real backend and deliver exact
  dimensions (the E10 gate), D75 canary + retention mechanics preserved
  (P13/P15); the gate statement lands in docs/design/future/image-generation.md
  (mocked graph-shape tests alone do not approve image delivery — the
  verification.md:28-33 layer-4 hook, no spec amendment).

**Implementation order and rationale:** M1-811, M1-812, M1-813, M1-814,
M1-815 are mutually independent (disjoint files; same-module serialization
handles the rest, P16). M1-816 last: its wiring fixture asserts the family
END state (P14) and its live probe asserts M1-812's crop on the real
backend. Files-to-touch per ticket are in each ticket's Approach.

## Controls to preserve (engineering-rules §10)

- **M1-801's strip and spool mechanics:** overflow-free bound arithmetic +
  IHDR-only pixel read (PngMetadataStrip.java:47-70); chunk-level drop with
  verbatim copy; atomic capacity refusal + temp-then-move write
  (ImageSpool.java:35-66); delete-on-completion + age eviction invariant.
  M1-811 changes only the bound VALUE; M1-814 changes only the absent-dir
  read. Tests pinning them (`refusesOversizedDimensions`,
  `refusesChunkDeclaringLengthNearIntMax`,
  `refusesWritesPastTheCapacityBound`,

## Verification strategy

Every pitfall maps to a named test/probe in the owning ticket; failure-mode
tests mandatory per ticket.

- P1 → `PngMetadataStripTest.shippedCeilingAcceptsTheMeasuredDefaultOutput`
  (M1-811, reads the shipped value) + review of the design-table row; the
  bound's DOS intent is pinned by the preserved `refusesOversizedDimensions`
  (a hostile IHDR still refuses at the raised value — failure-mode stays
  alive).
- P2 → M1-811 acceptance grep: the new WARN carries no prompt/graph; the
  forced over-ceiling handler test asserts the failure terminal + row.
- P3 → `promptLandsInExactlyOneGraphStringField` green unedited (M1-812).
- P4 → the authorized extension of
  `buildGraphHonoursAnExactPerJobOutputSize` + the new reproduction
  `resolutionGraphCarriesTheImageScaleCropInput` (RED on main).
- P5 → M1-813's four new arm tests each assert refund AND exactly one
  content-free row; `backendUnreachableRefunds` and
  `stopDuringQueueDepthReadWritesStoppedAuditRow` green unedited.
- P6/P7 → `ImageSpoolTest.absentSpoolDirIsAnEmptySpool` +
  `ImageSpoolSweeperTest.sweepCompletesWhenTheSpoolIsAbsent` (M1-814);
  eviction/capacity tests green unedited.
- P8 → M1-815 failure modes: deletion-join into a closed-list token still
  redacts + rows; deletion-join into a scaffolding marker still drops;
  ordering pinned by composition.
- P9 → `matchSetEqualsSpecClosedList` green unedited; `git diff` shows no
  CLOSED_LIST hunk.
- P10 → `LlmOutputSanitizerAuditRowIT`-shaped assertion: a config-key match
  lands one aggregated row with the exact count; the fail-loud path
  unchanged.
- P11 → the five-bundle rewording green under `BundleLoaderTest`; the
  duration-value pin green unedited; a new pin asserts no topic answer
  carries a raw `infochat.` token (RED on main).
- P12 → census doc + postcondition pin updates named in M1-815 acceptance.
- P13/P15 → M1-816 probe: configured-template assertions, canary prompt,
  history-clear + leftover + stdout checks.
- P14 → M1-816 wiring method RED before M1-811 / green after (blocked_by).

## Decomposition

Six tickets; each embeds its slice of this analysis.

- **M1-811 — image default output ceiling** (E8, both halves: the ceiling
  value and the silent catch share one catch block and one failure path —
  joined per the user instruction). blocked_by: none.
- **M1-812 — ComfyUI ImageScale crop input** (E10). blocked_by: none.
- **M1-813 — image audit completeness** (E13). blocked_by: none.
- **M1-814 — image spool sweeper absent dir** (E7). blocked_by: none.
- **M1-815 — sanitizer internal language leak** (E9). blocked_by: none.
- **M1-816 — image e2e release gate** (E11). blocked_by: M1-811, M1-812
  (fixture calibrated to the family end state, P14).

Joining rationale (user instruction): E8's config half and observability
half are ONE ticket (same catch block); E11 is NOT six one-to-one tickets —
each fix ticket lands its own regression net, and M1-816 carries only the
verification no unit test can (real-backend acceptance + shipped-config
wiring). E9 and E13 stay separate: different mechanisms (sanitizer quality
vs audit completeness), different fix surfaces, no shared test.

Order: 811/812/813/814/815 in any order (disjoint files; same-module
tickets serialize naturally), then 816. The report's five ticket-ready
follow-ups map: 1→M1-811, 2→M1-812, 3→M1-813, 4→M1-814, 5→M1-816; E9 is the
sixth (not in the report's list). The report's §"Additional tests
recommended" image items (every aspect ratio; sweeper after clean startup;
ComfyUI stop/restart) are absorbed by M1-816's probe, M1-814's tests, and
the E13 live verification already performed; its non-image items
(/summary window, second-client sanitizer probes) are out of scope.

Open item NOT absorbed (recorded for the user): M1-803 round-3's
RECOMMENDED-NEW-TICKET — the `jobStarted=true` refund net hole on the
timeout/stop arms (ImageCommandHandlerTest.java:574 family) — remains a
regression-net hole the shipped code does not have; none of these six
tickets touches those arms' refund logic, so it stays its own filing
decision. Likewise D-3's stale reference template
(prod/config/comfyui-workflow.json fails the Provider's own boot
validation) — candidate follow-up, not in this set (§1).
